stem.text: The amount of water in a storage tank changes at the rate \( A'(t) = 36 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} + 6 \) gallons per hour for \( 0 \le t \le 24 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 60 gallons of water in the tank, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 24 \) at which the amount A(t) of water is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 6.640, where A is 235.424 gallons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 24.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 60 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(36 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{12} \right)} + 6\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = 36 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} + 6 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 6.640 \) and \( t = 17.360 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 60 \), \( A(6.640) \approx 235.424 \), \( A(17.360) \approx 28.576 \), and \( A(24) = 60 + \int_{0}^{24} A'(s)\,ds = 204 \).
The largest candidate value is about 235.424, at the first critical point, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 6.640 \) hours.
